beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process updates it through shared DQ-CTM ticks.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense image field from the compact computation that updates it. The encoder converts the low-resolution input into the carrier features. Windowing partitions that carrier while keeping the spatial field dense. The DQ-CTM thought process reads and updates the windowed carrier. Recurrence returns to the thought process itself, with parameters shared across ticks. The decoder turns the final dense carrier back into the super-resolved image.

beats.intent: The carrier is dense because the encoder first makes a feature field and the window partition operates on that field without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier equation makes the dense state explicit before the thought process begins. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window partition takes that feature field as its input, so the token set stays tied to the carrier.

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; at 1.129 million parameters it is second largest among the five.
beats.claim: DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129M parameters in Table 1, compared with CARN 1.592M, IMDN 0.715M, RFDN 0.550M, and CATANet 0.535M.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison is a caveat to the compact-thought story. CATANet is the smallest reported model at zero point five three five million parameters. RFDN is almost the same size at zero point five five zero million. IMDN is larger at zero point seven one five million. DQ-CTM-SR reaches one point one two nine million, making it the second largest here. CARN is largest at one point five nine two million.
